name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q01 - Identification of allylic alcohols among unsaturated structures

questiontext.text: Which of the following compounds is classified as an allylic alcohol?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Understand the definition of an allylic alcohol
An allylic alcohol is an unsaturated alcohol in which the hydroxyl group (\( \mathrm{-OH} \)) is bonded to an \( sp^3 \)-hybridised carbon atom that is directly adjacent to a carbon-carbon double bond, referred to as an allylic carbon.

Step 2: Analyse the given structures
In prop-2-en-1-ol (\( \mathrm{CH_2=CH-CH_2OH} \)), the \( \mathrm{-OH} \) group is attached to an \( sp^3 \) carbon situated immediately next to the \( \mathrm{CH_2=CH-} \) unit, perfectly fulfilling the criteria of an allylic alcohol.
In contrast, \( \mathrm{CH_2=CH-OH} \) has the hydroxyl group attached directly to an \( sp^2 \)-hybridised doubly bonded carbon, making it a vinylic alcohol.
Benzyl alcohol (\( \mathrm{C_6H_5-CH_2OH} \)) contains an \( \mathrm{-OH} \) group bonded to an \( sp^3 \) carbon attached to an aromatic ring, classifying it as a benzylic alcohol.
Propan-1-ol (\( \mathrm{CH_3-CH_2-CH_2OH} \)) is a simple saturated aliphatic alcohol.

Step 3: State the final conclusion
Therefore, prop-2-en-1-ol (\( \mathrm{CH_2=CH-CH_2OH} \)) is the allylic alcohol.

answer.text: \( \mathrm{CH_2=CH-CH_2OH} \)
\( \mathrm{CH_2=CH-OH} \)
\( \mathrm{C_6H_5-CH_2OH} \)
\( \mathrm{CH_3-CH_2-CH_2OH} \)

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q02 - Classification of aliphatic monohydric alcohols by carbon degree

questiontext.text: What is the classification of 2-methylpropan-2-ol with respect to the degree of the carbon atom carrying the hydroxyl group?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Write the structural formula of the given compound
The chemical formula of 2-methylpropan-2-ol is \( \mathrm{(CH_3)_3C-OH} \). The central carbon atom is bonded to three methyl groups (\( \mathrm{-CH_3} \)) and one hydroxyl group (\( \mathrm{-OH} \)).

Step 2: Determine the degree of the carbon atom
A primary (\( 1^\circ \)) alcohol has the hydroxyl group bonded to a carbon attached to only one other carbon or none. A secondary (\( 2^\circ \)) alcohol has the hydroxyl-bearing carbon bonded to two other carbons. A tertiary (\( 3^\circ \)) alcohol has the hydroxyl-bearing carbon attached to three other carbon atoms.

Step 3: Conclude the classification
Because the carbon bearing the \( \mathrm{-OH} \) group is bonded directly to three carbon atoms, 2-methylpropan-2-ol is classified as a tertiary alcohol.

answer.text: Primary alcohol
Tertiary alcohol
Secondary alcohol
Dihydric alcohol

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q03 - Distinguishing vinylic from allylic and benzylic alcohols

questiontext.text: Which statement correctly describes the difference between a vinylic alcohol and an allylic alcohol?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Define vinylic alcohols
Vinylic alcohols contain the hydroxyl group (\( \mathrm{-OH} \)) bonded directly to a carbon atom of a carbon-carbon double bond, that is, to an \( sp^2 \)-hybridised vinylic carbon atom (for example, \( \mathrm{CH_2=CH-OH} \)).

Step 2: Define allylic alcohols
Allylic alcohols contain the hydroxyl group bonded to an \( sp^3 \)-hybridised carbon atom situated directly adjacent to a carbon-carbon double bond, termed an allylic carbon (for example, \( \mathrm{CH_2=CH-CH_2OH} \)).

Step 3: Compare the hybridisation and structural connectivity
The critical difference is that in vinylic alcohols, the hydroxyl group is bonded directly to an \( sp^2 \) carbon of the double bond, whereas in allylic alcohols it is bonded to an \( sp^3 \) carbon adjacent to the double bond.

answer.text: In a vinylic alcohol, the \( \mathrm{-OH} \) group is attached to an \( sp^3 \) hybridised carbon next to an aromatic ring, whereas in an allylic alcohol it is attached to a \( \mathrm{C=C} \) double bond.
Both vinylic and allylic alcohols have the \( \mathrm{-OH} \) group attached to an \( sp^3 \) hybridised carbon atom directly involved in a double bond.

In a vinylic alcohol, the \( \mathrm{-OH} \) group is attached directly to an \( sp^2 \) hybridised carbon of a \( \mathrm{C=C} \) double bond, whereas in an allylic alcohol it is attached to an \( sp^3 \) hybridised carbon adjacent to a \( \mathrm{C=C} \) double bond.
In an allylic alcohol, the \( \mathrm{-OH} \) group is attached directly to an \( sp^2 \) carbon, whereas in a vinylic alcohol it is attached to an aromatic ring.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q04 - IUPAC nomenclature of substituted cyclic alcohols

questiontext.text: According to the IUPAC system of nomenclature, how is a cyclopentane ring carrying an \( \mathrm{-OH} \) group at position 1 and a methyl group at an adjacent ring carbon named?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify the principal functional group and parent ring
The principal functional group is the hydroxyl group (\( \mathrm{-OH} \)), which gives the suffix '-ol'. The parent cyclic hydrocarbon is cyclopentane.

Step 2: Apply cyclic alcohol numbering rules
In cyclic alcohols, the ring carbon bonded to the \( \mathrm{-OH} \) group is automatically designated as carbon-1 (C-1). Numbering continues around the ring in the direction that gives the substituent the lowest possible locant.

Step 3: Assign locants and combine the name
The methyl group on the adjacent carbon receives locant 2. Thus, the systematic IUPAC name is 2-methylcyclopentanol.

answer.text: 1-Methylcyclopentan-2-ol
1-Hydroxy-2-methylcyclopentane
2-Hydroxymethylcyclopentane
2-Methylcyclopentanol

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q05 - IUPAC nomenclature of polyhydric alcohol glycerol

questiontext.text: What is the IUPAC name of glycerol, \( \mathrm{CH_2(OH)-CH(OH)-CH_2(OH)} \)?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify the longest continuous carbon chain
The parent chain consists of three carbon atoms, corresponding to propane.

Step 2: Identify the functional groups and suffix rule for polyhydric alcohols
There are three hydroxyl groups located on carbon atoms 1, 2, and 3. In naming polyhydric alcohols according to IUPAC rules, the terminal 'e' of the alkane name is retained, and the multiplicative suffix 'triol' is attached with appropriate locants.

Step 3: Assemble the IUPAC name
Retaining 'e' in propane and adding the locants and suffix gives propane-1,2,3-triol.

answer.text: Propane-1,2,3-triol
Propane-1,2,3-trial

Propanetriol-1,2,3

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q06 - Common and IUPAC naming of dihydroxybenzenes

questiontext.text: Which dihydroxy derivative of benzene corresponds to the common name resorcinol?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Recall the common dihydroxy derivatives of benzene
The three isomeric dihydroxy derivatives of benzene are catechol, resorcinol, and hydroquinone (or quinol).

Step 2: Match common names with IUPAC positions
Catechol is 1,2-dihydroxybenzene, named systematically as benzene-1,2-diol.
Resorcinol is 1,3-dihydroxybenzene, named systematically as benzene-1,3-diol.
Hydroquinone (quinol) is 1,4-dihydroxybenzene, named systematically as benzene-1,4-diol.

Step 3: State the final match
Resorcinol corresponds to benzene-1,3-diol.

answer.text: Benzene-1,2-diol
Benzene-1,3-diol
Benzene-1,4-diol
Benzene-1,2,3-triol

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q07 - IUPAC nomenclature of branched substituted aliphatic alcohols

questiontext.text: What is the IUPAC name of the compound \( \mathrm{CH_3-CH(Cl)-CH(CH_3)-CH(CH_3)-CH_2OH} \)?

Numbering begins from the end closest to the principal functional group (\( \mathrm{-OH} \)). Thus, the carbon bearing the hydroxyl group is designated C-1.

A chloro group is at C-4, and two methyl groups are at C-2 and C-3. Arranged alphabetically, 'chloro' precedes 'methyl'.
Combining prefixes, parent name, and suffix yields 4-chloro-2,3-dimethylpentan-1-ol.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q08 - IUPAC naming of substituted cyclohexyl ethers

questiontext.text: What is the systematic IUPAC name of a cyclohexane ring substituted with an ethoxy group (\( \mathrm{-OC_2H_5} \)) and a nitro group (\( \mathrm{-NO_2} \)) on adjacent carbons, numbered to give the lowest locant set with alphabetical priority?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify the parent hydrocarbon and substituents
The parent ring is cyclohexane. The substituents are an ethoxy group (\( \mathrm{-OC_2H_5} \)) and a nitro group (\( \mathrm{-NO_2} \)) at adjacent positions (locants 1 and 2).

Step 2: Apply the numbering rules for equivalent locant sets
Since the locant set is (1, 2) in either direction, priority for C-1 is determined alphabetically. The prefix 'ethoxy' precedes 'nitro' alphabetically. Therefore, carbon-1 is assigned to the carbon bearing the ethoxy group, and carbon-2 is assigned to the carbon bearing the nitro group.

Step 3: Combine into the final IUPAC name
The correct systematic name is 1-ethoxy-2-nitrocyclohexane.

answer.text: 2-Ethoxy-1-nitrocyclohexane

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q09 - Bond angle interpretation in methanol functional group

questiontext.text: In methanol, the \( \mathrm{C-O-H} \) bond angle is \( 108.9^\circ \), which is slightly less than the tetrahedral angle (\( 109^\circ 28' \)). What is the primary reason for this deviation?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify the electronic geometry of oxygen in alcohols
In alcohols such as methanol, the oxygen atom is \( sp^3 \) hybridised with four electron pairs: two bonding pairs and two unshared (lone) pairs.

Step 2: Apply VSEPR principles
According to Valence Shell Electron Pair Repulsion (VSEPR) theory, lone pair–lone pair repulsion is stronger than lone pair–bond pair and bond pair–bond pair repulsions. The repulsive interaction between the two unshared electron pairs on oxygen pushes the bonding pairs closer together.

Step 3: Formulate the final conclusion
This lone pair–lone pair repulsion compresses the \( \mathrm{C-O-H} \) bond angle slightly below the ideal tetrahedral angle of \( 109.5^\circ \) to \( 108.9^\circ \).

answer.text: Repulsion between the two unshared lone pairs of electrons on the oxygen atom
Steric repulsion between the bulky methyl group and the hydrogen atom
Attraction between the methyl group and the hydroxyl hydrogen atom
Hybridisation of the oxygen atom changing from \( sp^3 \) to \( sp^2 \)

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q10 - C-O bond length shortening in phenol relative to methanol

questiontext.text: The carbon–oxygen bond length in phenol is \( 136\text{ pm} \), whereas in methanol it is \( 142\text{ pm} \). Which factors account for the shorter \( \mathrm{C-O} \) bond length in phenol?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: State the experimental bond lengths
The \( \mathrm{C-O} \) bond length in methanol is \( 142\text{ pm} \), whereas in phenol it is shortened to \( 136\text{ pm} \).

Step 2: Analyse electronic and hybridisation effects in phenol
Two distinct factors are responsible for this bond shortening:
1. Resonance delocalisation: The unshared electron pair on oxygen enters into conjugation with the \( \pi \)-electron system of the aromatic ring, giving the carbon–oxygen bond partial double bond character.
2. Hybridisation: The ring carbon attached to oxygen is \( sp^2 \) hybridised (possessing greater \( s \)-character, \( 33.3\% \)), making it more electronegative and forming a shorter, stronger bond than the \( sp^3 \) hybridised carbon (\( 25\% \) \( s \)-character) in methanol.

Step 3: Combine both factors for the final answer
The reduction in bond length is due to partial double bond character from resonance conjugation together with the \( sp^2 \) hybridised state of the attached ring carbon atom.

answer.text: Hydrogen bonding between phenol molecules and steric hindrance of the benzene ring
Partial double bond character due to conjugation of the oxygen lone pair with the aromatic ring and the \( sp^2 \) hybridised state of the carbon atom
Greater electronegativity of oxygen in phenol and the \( sp^3 \) hybridised state of the aromatic carbon
Inductive electron donation by the phenyl ring and strong repulsion between lone pairs

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q11 - Bond angle widening in dialkyl ethers due to bulky groups

questiontext.text: The \( \mathrm{C-O-C} \) bond angle in methoxymethane (dimethyl ether) is \( 111.7^\circ \), which is noticeably greater than the tetrahedral angle (\( 109^\circ 28' \)). This bond angle enlargement is mainly caused by:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify the electron pair geometry of ether oxygen
In ethers, oxygen has four electron pairs (two bond pairs and two lone pairs) arranged in an approximately tetrahedral geometry.

Step 2: Analyse group interactions
Attached to the oxygen atom are two alkyl (methyl) groups. Because these alkyl groups are relatively bulky compared to hydrogen atoms, steric repulsive interactions between the two bulky groups force them further apart.

Step 3: Conclude the effect on the bond angle
This steric repulsion overpowers the lone-pair compression effect and widens the \( \mathrm{C-O-C} \) bond angle to \( 111.7^\circ \), which is greater than the tetrahedral angle.

answer.text: Strong attraction between the two methyl groups
Partial triple bond character between carbon and oxygen
Repulsive steric interactions between the two bulky alkyl groups
Conversion of the oxygen hybridisation to \( sp \)

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q12 - Markovnikov hydration of propene to propan-2-ol

questiontext.text: When propene reacts with water in the presence of an acid catalyst (\( \mathrm{H^+} \)), what is the major alcohol formed according to Markovnikov's rule?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Recall the acid-catalysed hydration reaction
The reaction of an unsymmetrical alkene with water in the presence of dilute mineral acid proceeds by electrophilic addition following Markovnikov's rule.

Step 2: Apply Markovnikov's rule
During electrophilic addition to propene (\( \mathrm{CH_3-CH=CH_2} \)), the proton (\( \mathrm{H^+} \)) adds to the less substituted \( sp^2 \) carbon (carrying more hydrogen atoms) to generate the more stable secondary carbocation: \( \mathrm{CH_3-\overset{+}{C}H-CH_3} \).

Step 3: Attack of nucleophile and proton transfer
Water then attacks this secondary carbocation, followed by loss of a proton, yielding propan-2-ol (\( \mathrm{CH_3-CH(OH)-CH_3} \)).

Step 4: Conclude the major product
The major product is propan-2-ol.

answer.text: Propan-1-ol
Propane-1,2-diol
Ethanol
Propan-2-ol

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q13 - Acid-catalysed hydration of branched alkene with carbocation rearrangement

questiontext.text: When 3,3-dimethylbut-1-ene is subjected to acid-catalysed hydration (\( \mathrm{H_2O / H^+} \)), the major product formed is:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Write initial protonation of the alkene
Protonation of 3,3-dimethylbut-1-ene (\( \mathrm{(CH_3)_3C-CH=CH_2} \)) by \( \mathrm{H^+} \) occurs at the terminal carbon in accordance with Markovnikov's rule to produce a secondary carbocation: \( \mathrm{(CH_3)_3C-\overset{+}{C}H-CH_3} \).

Step 2: Evaluate carbocation rearrangement
The initially formed secondary carbocation has an adjacent quaternary carbon carrying three methyl groups. A 1,2-methyl shift occurs from the adjacent carbon to the carbocation centre, converting the less stable secondary carbocation into a more stable tertiary carbocation: \( \mathrm{CH_3-\overset{+}{C}(CH_3)-CH(CH_3)-CH_3} \).

Step 3: Nucleophilic attack and deprotonation
Water attacks the tertiary carbocation at C-2, followed by the loss of a proton to give the rearranged alcohol: 2,3-dimethylbutan-2-ol.

Step 4: State the final major product
Thus, the major product of the reaction is 2,3-dimethylbutan-2-ol.

answer.text: 2,3-Dimethylbutan-2-ol
3,3-Dimethylbutan-2-ol
3,3-Dimethylbutan-1-ol
2,3-Dimethylbutan-1-ol

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q14 - Hydroboration-oxidation regiochemical outcome for propene

questiontext.text: Propene is treated with diborane followed by oxidation with alkaline hydrogen peroxide (\( \mathrm{H_2O_2 / OH^-} \)). What is the final alcohol obtained?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify the overall reaction type
The sequence of diborane treatment followed by alkaline hydrogen peroxide is hydroboration-oxidation, first reported by H.C. Brown.

Step 2: Analyse the addition of borane
Addition of borane (\( \mathrm{BH_3} \)) to the double bond takes place such that the boron atom attaches to the \( sp^2 \) carbon carrying the greater number of hydrogen atoms (the terminal carbon) to form tripropylborane, \( \mathrm{(CH_3-CH_2-CH_2)_3B} \).

Step 3: Oxidation and hydrolysis
Oxidation of tripropylborane with alkaline \( \mathrm{H_2O_2} \) hydrolyses the carbon-boron bonds, replacing boron with a hydroxyl group with complete retention of regiochemistry, yielding propan-1-ol and boric acid (\( \mathrm{B(OH)_3} \)).

Step 4: Conclude the final product
The net transformation corresponds to anti-Markovnikov addition of water, yielding propan-1-ol in excellent yield.

answer.text: Propan-2-ol
Propan-1-ol
Propanoic acid
Ethane-1,2-diol

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q15 - Regioselective basis of borane addition to alkenes

questiontext.text: During the hydroboration of an unsymmetrical alkene, why does the boron atom attach preferentially to the less substituted sp2 carbon atom?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Analyse the transition state of hydroboration
Hydroboration involves a concerted four-centre cyclic transition state where the boron-hydrogen bond adds across the carbon-carbon double bond.

Step 2: Evaluate steric and electronic factors
Because the boron group is larger than a hydrogen atom, placing boron at the less hindered, less substituted carbon minimizes steric repulsion. Electronically, partial positive charge development during the addition is better stabilized at the more substituted adjacent carbon.

Step 3: State the final conclusion
Consequently, the boron atom attaches to the carbon carrying the greater number of hydrogen atoms due to combined steric and electronic advantages.

answer.text: Boron is more electronegative than hydrogen and acts as a nucleophile
The reaction proceeds via a free carbocation at the terminal carbon
Both steric hindrance is minimized at the less substituted carbon and the transition state is electronically stabilized
The reaction involves Markovnikov addition of a halide ion

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q16 - Chemoselective reduction of keto-ester using sodium borohydride

questiontext.text: What is the product when methyl 2-(2-oxocyclohexyl)acetate (a compound containing both a cyclic ketone and an ester group) is treated with \( \mathrm{NaBH_4} \)?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify the functional groups in the starting molecule
The molecule possesses two carbonyl-containing functional groups: a cyclic ketone and an aliphatic ester.

Step 2: Recall the reducing selectivity of sodium borohydride
Sodium borohydride (\( \mathrm{NaBH_4} \)) is a mild and chemoselective reducing agent that readily reduces aldehydes to primary alcohols and ketones to secondary alcohols, but does not reduce esters or carboxylic acids under ordinary conditions.

Step 3: Determine the product of the reaction
Therefore, the ketone carbonyl is selectively reduced to a secondary hydroxyl group, while the ester carbonyl group remains completely intact.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q17 - Commercial reduction route of carboxylic acids to alcohols via esters

questiontext.text: Although lithium aluminium hydride (\( \mathrm{LiAlH_4} \)) reduces carboxylic acids to primary alcohols in excellent yield, it is not used commercially for large-scale production. How are carboxylic acids commercially converted into alcohols?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Understand the economic limitation of lithium aluminium hydride
Lithium aluminium hydride (\( \mathrm{LiAlH_4} \)) is a powerful reducing agent that cleanly reduces carboxylic acids to primary alcohols, but it is expensive and hazardous for bulk commercial manufacturing.

Step 2: Identify the commercial chemical sequence
Commercially, carboxylic acids are first esterified with an alcohol in the presence of an acid catalyst: \( \mathrm{RCOOH + R'OH \xrightarrow{H^+} RCOOR' + H_2O} \).

Step 3: Identify the subsequent catalytic reduction
The resulting ester is then reduced smoothly by catalytic hydrogenation using hydrogen gas in the presence of a metal catalyst: \( \mathrm{RCOOR' \xrightarrow[Catalyst]{H_2} RCH_2OH + R'OH} \).

Step 4: State the final answer
Hence, commercial production relies on conversion of the acid to an ester followed by catalytic hydrogenation.

answer.text: By first converting the carboxylic acid into an ester followed by catalytic hydrogenation
By direct reduction with sodium borohydride (\( \mathrm{NaBH_4} \)) in water
By heating the acid with concentrated sulphuric acid at high temperature
By treating the carboxylic acid directly with zinc amalgam and concentrated hydrochloric acid

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q18 - Classification of alcohols prepared from Grignard reagents and carbonyls

questiontext.text: Which class of alcohol is produced when a Grignard reagent reacts with methanal (formaldehyde) followed by hydrolysis?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Write the general Grignard reaction with methanal
The reaction of a Grignard reagent (\( \mathrm{RMgX} \)) with methanal (\( \mathrm{HCHO} \)) proceeds by nucleophilic addition to give a magnesium alkoxide adduct: \( \mathrm{HCHO + RMgX \rightarrow R-CH_2-OMgX} \).

Step 2: Analyse the product after hydrolysis
Hydrolysis of this adduct gives: \( \mathrm{R-CH_2-OMgX + H_2O \rightarrow R-CH_2OH + Mg(OH)X} \).

Step 3: Classify the resulting alcohol
The product \( \mathrm{R-CH_2OH} \) contains the hydroxyl group attached to a \( \mathrm{-CH_2-} \) carbon (bonded to only one alkyl group), which defines a primary alcohol.

answer.text: Secondary alcohol
Primary alcohol

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q19 - Grignard synthesis of tertiary alcohol from ketone

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify the reactants
The ketone is propanone, \( \mathrm{CH_3-CO-CH_3} \), and the Grignard reagent is methylmagnesium bromide, \( \mathrm{CH_3MgBr} \).

Step 2: Trace the nucleophilic addition step
The nucleophilic methyl group from \( \mathrm{CH_3MgBr} \) attacks the carbonyl carbon of propanone to form the magnesium alkoxide intermediate: \( \mathrm{(CH_3)_3C-OMgBr} \).

Subsequent hydrolysis yields \( \mathrm{(CH_3)_3C-OH} \) along with \( \mathrm{Mg(OH)Br} \).

The structure \( \mathrm{(CH_3)_3C-OH} \) has a three-carbon parent chain with a methyl substituent and a hydroxyl group at C-2, giving the systematic IUPAC name 2-methylpropan-2-ol.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q20 - Preparation of cyclohexylmethanol via Grignard addition to methanal

questiontext.text: Which combination of reactants will synthesise cyclohexylmethanol upon reaction followed by hydrolysis?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify the target structure
Cyclohexylmethanol has the formula \( \mathrm{C_6H_{11}-CH_2OH} \), which is a primary alcohol containing a cyclohexyl ring attached to a \( \mathrm{-CH_2OH} \) group.

Step 2: Recall the method for preparing primary alcohols via Grignard reagents
A primary alcohol of the form \( \mathrm{R-CH_2OH} \) is synthesised by the addition of a Grignard reagent (\( \mathrm{RMgX} \)) to methanal (\( \mathrm{HCHO} \)).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q21 - Industrial preparation of phenol from chlorobenzene via Dow process

questiontext.text: In the industrial preparation of phenol from chlorobenzene (Dow's process), what are the required reaction conditions?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Understand the low reactivity of haloarenes
In chlorobenzene, the \( \mathrm{C-Cl} \) bond has partial double bond character due to resonance, making nucleophilic substitution difficult under ordinary conditions.

Step 2: State the industrial reaction conditions
To replace the chlorine atom, chlorobenzene is fused with sodium hydroxide under drastic conditions: a temperature of \( 623\text{ K} \) and a pressure of \( 320\text{ atm} \) (or \( 300\text{–}320\text{ atm} \)).

Step 3: Acidification of the phenoxide intermediate
This reaction produces sodium phenoxide (\( \mathrm{C_6H_5ONa} \)), which upon subsequent acidification with dilute hydrochloric acid yields phenol.

answer.text: Fusion with \( \mathrm{NaOH} \) at \( 623\text{ K} \) and \( 320\text{ atm} \) followed by acidification
Treatment with aqueous \( \mathrm{NaOH} \) at room temperature and \( 1\text{ atm} \)
Heating with concentrated \( \mathrm{HCl} \) at \( 373\text{ K} \)

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q22 - Preparation of phenol from benzene via sulphonation and alkali fusion

questiontext.text: What is the sequence of reagents required to prepare phenol from benzene via benzenesulphonic acid?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Sulphonation of benzene
Benzene is treated with oleum (fuming sulphuric acid) to form benzenesulphonic acid: \( \mathrm{C_6H_6 + SO_3 / H_2SO_4 \rightarrow C_6H_5SO_3H} \).

Step 2: Fusion with molten alkali
Benzenesulphonic acid is heated with molten sodium hydroxide to convert the sulphonic acid group into sodium phenoxide (\( \mathrm{C_6H_5ONa} \)).

Step 3: Acidification
Acidification of sodium phenoxide with dilute acid liberates free phenol (\( \mathrm{C_6H_5OH} \)).

answer.text: Concentrated \( \mathrm{HCl} \), followed by sodium metal, then water
Oleum, followed by heating with molten \( \mathrm{NaOH} \), and finally acidification with dilute acid

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q23 - Preparation of phenol from aniline via diazonium salt hydrolysis

questiontext.text: Aniline is treated with \( \mathrm{NaNO_2 + HCl} \) at \( 273\text{–}278\text{ K} \) to form benzenediazonium chloride. What reagent and condition convert this diazonium salt to phenol?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Recall the diazotisation reaction

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q32 - Acidity ranking of primary secondary and tertiary alcohols

Greater resonance stabilization of phenoxide relative to un-ionised phenol shifts the ionisation equilibrium forward, making phenol approximately a million times more acidic than ethanol.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q35 - Substituent effects and pKa values of nitrophenols versus cresols

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q44 - Dehydration of tertiary alcohol over heated copper at 573 K

questiontext.text: When vapours of 2-methylpropan-2-ol are passed over heated copper catalyst at \( 573\text{ K} \), what reaction occurs and what is the major organic product?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Recall the action of heated copper at 573 K on primary and secondary alcohols
When vapours of primary alcohols pass over copper at 573 K, dehydrogenation occurs to yield aldehydes.
With secondary alcohols, dehydrogenation occurs to yield ketones.

Step 2: Analyse the structure and reactivity of tertiary alcohols
Tertiary alcohols like 2-methylpropan-2-ol, \( \mathrm{(CH_3)_3C-OH} \), do not possess an \( \alpha \)-hydrogen atom on the hydroxyl-bearing carbon, preventing dehydrogenation.

Step 3: Determine the reaction pathway for tertiary alcohols
Under these high-temperature conditions over copper at \( 573\text{ K} \), tertiary alcohols undergo dehydration rather than dehydrogenation, eliminating a molecule of water to yield an alkene: \( \mathrm{(CH_3)_3C-OH \xrightarrow{Cu, 573\text{ K}} (CH_3)_2C=CH_2 + H_2O} \).

Step 4: State the final conclusion
The reaction is dehydration, and the product is 2-methylpropene.

Oxidation takes place to form 2-methylpropanoic acid
Cleavage takes place to form ethanal and methanol

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q45 - Industrial synthesis of methanol and biological toxicity mechanism

questiontext.text: Methanol is manufactured industrially by catalytic hydrogenation of carbon monoxide over a \( \mathrm{ZnO - Cr_2O_3} \) catalyst at \( 200\text{–}300\text{ atm} \) and \( 573\text{–}673\text{ K} \). In the human body, why is ingestion of methanol fatal, and how is it medically treated?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Understand biological oxidation of methanol
In the human body, methanol is oxidised by alcohol dehydrogenase first to methanal (formaldehyde) and then to methanoic acid (formic acid). These metabolites attack the optic nerve causing blindness and disrupt cellular respiration leading to death.

Step 2: Understand the antidote mechanism
Ethanol has a much higher affinity for alcohol dehydrogenase than methanol. By administering intravenous infusions of diluted ethanol, the enzyme is competitively occupied (swamped). This prevents the oxidation of methanol, giving the kidneys sufficient time to safely excrete intact methanol.

Step 3: State the final conclusion
Toxicity is caused by conversion to methanal and methanoic acid, and competitive treatment utilizes ethanol infusions.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q46 - Enzymatic fermentation of sugars and denaturation of ethanol

questiontext.text: During commercial ethanol production by fermentation of molasses, which two enzymes catalyse the sequential conversion of sucrose to ethanol, and why is commercial alcohol denatured?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify the sequential enzymes in fermentation
1. Invertase hydrolyses sucrose (in molasses or fruits) into an equimolar mixture of glucose and fructose: \( \mathrm{C_{12}H_{22}O_{11} + H_2O \xrightarrow{Invertase} C_6H_{12}O_6 + C_6H_{12}O_6} \).
2. Zymase (present in yeast) ferments glucose and fructose under anaerobic conditions into ethanol and carbon dioxide: \( \mathrm{C_6H_{12}O_6 \xrightarrow{Zymase} 2\,C_2H_5OH + 2\,CO_2} \).

Step 2: Identify the fermentation limit
Fermentation ceases when the alcohol concentration reaches approximately 14% because zymase is inhibited.

Step 3: Explain denaturation of commercial alcohol
To prevent the misuse of industrial alcohol for drinking purposes, it is denatured by adding copper sulphate (to give a distinctive colour) and pyridine (a foul-smelling liquid).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q47 - Mechanistic pathway and limitations of bimolecular dehydration of alcohols

questiontext.text: Why is the preparation of ethers by acid-catalysed dehydration of secondary or tertiary alcohols generally unsuccessful?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify the mechanism of ether formation from alcohols
The formation of symmetrical ethers by dehydration of alcohols is an \( \mathrm{S_N2} \) process involving nucleophilic attack by an unprotonated alcohol molecule on a protonated alcohol molecule.

Step 2: Evaluate the behaviour of secondary and tertiary alcohols
For secondary and tertiary alcohols, steric hindrance around the carbon centre disfavours \( \mathrm{S_N2} \) substitution. Furthermore, secondary and tertiary carbocations form readily and eliminate a proton via the \( \mathrm{E1} \) pathway to give stable, substituted alkenes.

Step 3: Conclude the limitation
Because elimination dominates heavily over nucleophilic substitution for secondary and tertiary alcohols, alkenes are produced as the primary products rather than ethers.

Because ethers formed from secondary and tertiary alcohols explode spontaneously at room temperature

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q48 - Williamson synthesis design for tert-butyl ethyl ether

questiontext.text: Which combination of reagents provides the appropriate synthetic pathway for the preparation of tert-butyl ethyl ether via Williamson ether synthesis?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Recall the mechanism of Williamson ether synthesis
Williamson ether synthesis involves an \( \mathrm{S_N2} \) displacement of a halide ion from an alkyl halide by an alkoxide ion: \( \mathrm{R-X + R'-O^- \rightarrow R-O-R' + X^-} \).

Step 2: Analyse the substrate requirement for SN2
\( \mathrm{S_N2} \) reactions proceed efficiently only with primary (or methyl) alkyl halides. If a tertiary alkyl halide (such as 2-bromo-2-methylpropane) is treated with a strong base/nucleophile like sodium ethoxide, base-induced elimination (\( \mathrm{E2} \)) takes place exclusively to produce 2-methylpropene.

Step 3: Design the correct combination
To form tert-butyl ethyl ether, the bulky tert-butyl group must reside on the alkoxide (sodium tert-butoxide), and the ethyl group must be supplied as a primary alkyl halide (bromoethane): \( \mathrm{(CH_3)_3C-O^-Na^+ + CH_3CH_2Br \rightarrow (CH_3)_3C-O-CH_2CH_3 + NaBr} \).

Ethanol and 2-methylprop-1-ene in neutral water

Sodium tert-butoxide and bromoethane

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q49 - Elimination pathway of tertiary alkyl halide with sodium alkoxide

questiontext.text: What is the exclusive organic product formed when 2-bromo-2-methylpropane is reacted with sodium methoxide (\( \mathrm{CH_3ONa} \))?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Identify the nature of the reactants
The substrate is 2-bromo-2-methylpropane, \( \mathrm{(CH_3)_3C-Br} \), a tertiary alkyl halide. The reagent is sodium methoxide, \( \mathrm{CH_3ONa} \), which is both a nucleophile and a strong Bronsted base.

Step 2: Evaluate substitution versus elimination
Tertiary alkyl halides are extremely hindered, preventing backside nucleophilic attack required for \( \mathrm{S_N2} \) substitution. Instead, the strongly basic methoxide ion abstracts a \( \beta \)-proton from one of the methyl groups, resulting in clean \( \mathrm{E2} \) elimination.

Step 3: Write the reaction equation
\( \mathrm{(CH_3)_3C-Br + CH_3ONa \rightarrow CH_3-C(CH_3)=CH_2 + NaBr + CH_3OH} \).

Step 4: Conclude the final organic product
The exclusive organic product is 2-methylpropene; no ether is formed.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q50 - Regioselective cleavage of primary mixed ether with concentrated HI

questiontext.text: When 1-methoxypropane (\( \mathrm{CH_3-O-CH_2CH_2CH_3} \)) is heated with an equimolar quantity of concentrated \( \mathrm{HI} \), what are the cleavage products?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Write the protonation step
Reaction begins with protonation of the ether oxygen by \( \mathrm{HI} \) to form an oxonium ion: \( \mathrm{CH_3-\overset{+}{O}(H)-CH_2CH_2CH_3} \).

Step 2: Identify the mechanism of nucleophilic attack
Both attached alkyl groups (methyl and n-propyl) are primary. Therefore, cleavage proceeds via an \( \mathrm{S_N2} \) mechanism where the iodide ion (\( \mathrm{I^-} \)) acts as a nucleophile.

Step 3: Determine the site of nucleophilic attack
In an \( \mathrm{S_N2} \) process, nucleophilic attack occurs preferentially at the least sterically hindered carbon atom. The methyl carbon is significantly less hindered than the primary carbon of the propyl chain. Hence, \( \mathrm{I^-} \) attacks the methyl group, displacing propan-1-ol as the leaving group: \( \mathrm{I^- + CH_3-\overset{+}{O}(H)-CH_2CH_2CH_3 \rightarrow CH_3I + CH_3CH_2CH_2OH} \).

Step 4: State the final products
The products are iodomethane and propan-1-ol.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q51 - SN1 cleavage of ether containing tertiary alkyl group with HI

questiontext.text: When tert-butyl methyl ether, \( \mathrm{(CH_3)_3C-O-CH_3} \), is treated with concentrated \( \mathrm{HI} \), what are the primary reaction products?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Protonate the ether oxygen
Protonation by \( \mathrm{HI} \) forms the oxonium ion: \( \mathrm{(CH_3)_3C-\overset{+}{O}(H)-CH_3} \).

Step 2: Evaluate the cleavage pathway (SN1 vs SN2)
When one of the alkyl groups is tertiary, departure of the neutral leaving group (\( \mathrm{CH_3OH} \)) generates an exceptionally stable tertiary carbocation: \( \mathrm{(CH_3)_3C^+} \). The reaction proceeds via an \( \mathrm{S_N1} \) mechanism rather than \( \mathrm{S_N2} \).

Step 3: Attack of the halide nucleophile
In the subsequent fast step, the iodide ion (\( \mathrm{I^-} \)) combines with the tertiary carbocation: \( \mathrm{(CH_3)_3C^+ + I^- \rightarrow (CH_3)_3C-I} \).

Step 4: State the final products
The cleavage yields tert-butyl iodide and methanol.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_MCQ_Q52 - Cleavage of anisole with HI to phenol and iodomethane

questiontext.text: When anisole (methoxybenzene) is heated with concentrated \( \mathrm{HI} \), it cleaves into phenol and iodomethane. Why does the reaction not yield iodobenzene and methanol?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Trace the protonation of anisole
Protonation of anisole by \( \mathrm{HI} \) gives methylphenyl oxonium ion: \( \mathrm{C_6H_5-\overset{+}{O}(H)-CH_3} \).

Step 2: Compare the two carbon-oxygen bonds
The bond between oxygen and the phenyl carbon has partial double bond character because the oxygen lone pair is in conjugation with the benzene ring. Furthermore, the phenyl carbon is \( sp^2 \) hybridised and holds electrons tightly.
In contrast, the bond between oxygen and the aliphatic methyl carbon is a normal single bond with an \( sp^3 \) hybridised carbon.

Step 3: Evaluate nucleophilic attack by iodide
The iodide ion (\( \mathrm{I^-} \)) attacks the less hindered \( sp^3 \) methyl carbon via an \( \mathrm{S_N2} \) mechanism, breaking the weaker \( \mathrm{O-CH_3} \) bond to generate \( \mathrm{CH_3I} \) and leaving behind phenol (\( \mathrm{C_6H_5OH} \)).
Phenol does not react further with \( \mathrm{HI} \) because the \( sp^2 \) carbon cannot undergo nucleophilic displacement.

Step 4: Conclude the final explanation
Thus, the partial double bond character of the \( \mathrm{O-C_6H_5} \) bond and resistance of \( sp^2 \) carbon to substitution ensure that only phenol and iodomethane are formed.

Phenol spontaneously reacts with \( \mathrm{HI} \) to form iodobenzene at room temperature
The \( \mathrm{O-CH_3} \) bond is stronger than the \( \mathrm{O-C_6H_5} \) bond due to hyperconjugation
